headline: MP HC: Co-op society's interest from co-op bank deposits eligible for s.80P(2)(d) deduction
reference: Pr. CIT-1 vs M.P. Matsya Mahasangh Sahkari, ITA No. 31 of 2026, Madhya Pradesh High Court (Jabalpur)
summary_points: Issue: whether interest earned by a co-operative society on investments with a co-operative bank qualifies for deduction under Section 80P(2)(d).
Held: Section 80P(4) bars deduction only where the assessee itself is a co-operative bank; it does not deny deduction on interest earned from a co-operative bank.
Court noted Section 2(19) treats all co-operative societies alike, and a contrary reading would defeat the purpose of Section 80P.
Revenue's appeal against the ITAT Indore order (AY 2017-18, interest of ₹5,92,55,175) was dismissed; the Tribunal's order was upheld.
who_is_affected: Co-operative societies (non-banking) that earn interest on deposits or investments with co-operative banks, and the Revenue officers assessing them.
action_required: Co-operative societies may rely on this ruling to support s.80P(2)(d) claims in pending assessments and appeals, subject to checking the full judgment and any contrary rulings.

social.linkedin:
Madhya Pradesh High Court on Section 80P(2)(d): interest earned by a co-operative society from its investments in a co-operative bank is deductible.

In PCIT-1 vs M.P. Matsya Mahasangh Sahkari (ITA No. 31 of 2026, decided 17 November 2026), the Revenue had disallowed a deduction of ₹5,92,55,175 for AY 2017-18, relying on Section 80P(4).

The Court held that Section 80P(4) excludes only those assessees that are themselves co-operative banks. It does not take away the deduction for a co-operative society earning interest from a co-operative bank. Section 2(19) makes no distinction between societies by their activity, and the Court said a contrary reading would defeat the purpose of Section 80P.

The appeal was dismissed and the ITAT Indore order was upheld.

Practical impact: co-operative societies with deposits in co-operative banks have strong support for such claims in pending assessments and appeals.

Please verify with the official judgment before relying on it.
